guarantees.claim: In the generate block gen_no_key_share1_reg, unused_key_share1 is driven by XOR reduction of reg2hw.key_share1.
guarantees.cond: when the enclosing generate condition (not visible) selects this block

guarantees.claim: When EnMasking is true or SwKeyMasked is false, sw_key_data is assigned the full value of sw_key_data_reg (forwarded as is).
When EnMasking is false and SwKeyMasked is true, sw_key_data[0] is assigned sw_key_data_reg[0] XOR sw_key_data_reg[1]; sw_key_data[1] is left undriven.
wait_timer_prescaler and wait_timer_limit are driven by CSR fields entropy_period.prescaler.q and entropy_period.wait_timer.q respectively.
entropy_refresh_req is asserted only when cmd.entropy_req.q and its qualifier .qe are both high.
entropy_seed_update is driven by cmd.entropy_seed.qe; entropy_seed_data is driven by cmd.entropy_seed.q.
entropy_hash_threshold is driven by the shadowed register field entropy_refresh_threshold_shadowed.q.
hw2reg.entropy_refresh_hash_cnt.de is tied to 1'b1; .d is continuously driven by entropy_hash_cnt.
entropy_hash_clr is asserted when cmd.hash_cnt_clr.qe and .q are both high.
entropy_ready is high only when cfg_shadowed.entropy_ready.q and its qualifier .qe are both high.
entropy_mode is driven by type-cast of cfg_shadowed.entropy_mode.q; entropy_fast_process is driven by cfg_shadowed.entropy_fast_process.q.
cfg_msg_mask is driven by cfg_shadowed.msg_mask.q; msg_mask_en is asserted when cfg_msg_mask, msg_valid, and msg_ready are all high.
cfg_en_unsupported_modestrength is driven by the corresponding shadowed register field.

assumptions.claim: reg2hw fields .q and .qe follow the expected CSR ownership and shadowing protocol without glitches.
assumptions.cond: when a field’s qe is used as a qualifier
assumptions.risk: If .qe is asserted spuriously (e.g., due to CSR write timing), qualified signals like entropy_refresh_req or entropy_ready may falsely trigger operations leading to incorrect entropy injection or state change.

assumptions.claim: msg_valid and msg_ready signals are properly driven by the message interface and are deasserted during non-data phases.
assumptions.risk: If msg_valid or msg_ready glitches or is stuck high, msg_mask_en could be asserted unintentionally, enabling the message LFSR at wrong times and corrupting mask generation.

assumptions.claim: entropy_hash_cnt is a valid counter that can be sampled every cycle without missing updates or metadata hazards.
assumptions.risk: If the counter is not glitch-free or has downstream dependencies (e.g., synchronized to a different clock), the continuously sampled register may capture intermediate or spurious values, causing SW to read an invalid hash count.

uncertain_points.claim: unused_key_share1 is generated by XOR reduction of reg2hw.key_share1 in the gen_no_key_share1_reg block, but no consumer of this signal is visible in the chunk.
uncertain_points.cond: when the enclosing parameter condition activates gen_no_key_share1_reg
uncertain_points.risk: If the signal truly has no user, it may be left dangling, causing synthesis warnings or unintended removal; if used elsewhere, the missing connection could indicate a missing binding or hidden dependency.

uncertain_points.claim: In the gen_key_unmask branch (EnMasking=0, SwKeyMasked=1), only sw_key_data[0] is assigned, leaving sw_key_data[1] undriven.
uncertain_points.cond: when masking disabled and key is provided in two shares
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream logic expecting a fully driven key bus (both share elements) may read X or stale values from sw_key_data[1], potentially leading to key corruption, incorrect digest, or security vulnerability if the second share is used as a blinding factor elsewhere.

uncertain_points.claim: hw2reg.entropy_refresh_hash_cnt.de is tied to 1, causing the register to sample entropy_hash_cnt on every cycle without any SW write protection or read-side handshake.
uncertain_points.risk: If SW reads the register while the counter is being updated, the read could return a partially updated value (depending on bus width) or a value that is inconsistent with the actual hash state, leading to erroneous entropy monitoring decisions.

uncertain_points.claim: msg_mask_en depends on external signals msg_valid and msg_ready whose mutual timing and deassertion protocol are not enforced within this chunk.
uncertain_points.risk: If the upstream handshake protocol allows msg_valid to remain high after message transfer or msg_ready to stay high during idle, msg_mask_en could be spuriously active, causing the LFSR to run outside the intended data window and possibly injecting undesired mask values into the pipeline.
